1. **`orders.ts` — `Book.strikeOff`**: strikes an order using `delete`, which leaves a hole instead of shrinking the array. `count()` still reports the old length and `orders()` surfaces the hole as `undefined`, so the book isn't actually shorter — violating "the book is the shorter for it."

All 35 existing tests pass, and running `office.ts` now writes up all four messages including CARLISLE, footed correctly at "4 messages, 72d".

## Fix

The bug was in `Cutter._flush` in `messages.ts`. When the drum ran dry, any tape held after the last mark — the day's final message, which has no mark following it because nothing was sent after it — was silently thrown away (`this.held = ""`) instead of being read off and pushed downstream. That's why a fourth, unmarked message on the tape never reached the sheet.

The fix reads off whatever is still held (if non-empty) and pushes it as a `Wire`, exactly as the running `_transform` loop does for every marked message, before clearing the buffer. Nothing else — pricing, formatting, the footer's counting logic, or any existing test — changed.
